song.title: Les feuilles mortes
song.story: Les feuilles mortes invites us into a world of autumn, lost love, and the persistence of memory. Rather than treating the song as a museum piece, today’s note considers how its words, performance, and arrangement work together.
song.context: Released in 1946, the recording belongs to a changing French-language music landscape. Its period details matter, but the emotional situation remains immediate enough to travel across generations.
song.listenFor: Listen first to Yves Montand’s phrasing: where the voice presses forward, where it pauses, and how the accompaniment changes the emotional temperature. A second hearing often reveals the song’s careful balance between narrative and refrain.
song.legacy: The song endures because its central idea—autumn, lost love, and the persistence of memory—is specific enough to feel lived-in and open enough for new listeners to recognize themselves in it.
